content:
**Visual observations:**
- Young soybean seedlings in greenhouse pots
- Leaves show clear green-to-yellow mottling/blotchiness — irregular light yellowish-green patches on a darker green background
- Mild leaf distortion/puckering visible on affected leaves
- No necrotic spots, no fungal structures, no stem lesions, no brown spots

**Candidate narrowing:**
- The mottled pattern (light/dark green mosaic) on young upper canopy leaves points strongly to viral disease
- **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus**: "Green to yellow mottling (blotchiness) of younger leaves in the upper canopy; in severe cases leaves may show puckering and distortion" — matches very well
- **Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus**: describes dark green, brittle, wrinkled, curled leaves with interveinal yellowing — the leaves here are not particularly dark/brittle
- **Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus**: requires yellow spots along veins progressing to red-brown necrotic lesions — no necrosis present
- **Tobacco_Streak_Virus**: bud blight, shepherd's crook, dead streaks at nodes — not matching

The green-to-yellow blotchy mottling on young leaves without necrosis or vein-specific symptoms is the hallmark of BPMV.
